newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts expect NorScan stocks to fall in Mar.
newsitem.headline: Analysts expect NorScan stocks to fall in Mar.

text.p: Forestry sector analysts said on Friday that they expected North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks to have fallen in March.
"The figures that are around indicate that stocks have fallen by between 140,000 and 160,000 tonnes," said Soren Nordin, market analyst at Modo Paper.
"If this were the case, then the stock levels are lower than a lot of people in the market expected."
Market analysts told Reuters that stocks in Canada and the U.S. fell by 59,000 tonnes to around 903,000 tonnes and by 95,000 tonnes to about 629,000 tonnes respectively last month.
Stocks in Finland were expected to have increased by 5,000 tonnes to 117,000 tonnes.
Swedish stocks were expected to be unchanged at around 267,000 tonnes.
"It is possible that stocks in Sweden have fallen a litte after a big stop at SCA's factory in Ostrand," said one analyst.
Stock levels in Norway are also unclear.

Some analysts told Reuters that they thought levels had risen a little in Norway while others expected a slight dip. On average the analysts were not expecting levels to have changed much from the previous month's level of 43,000 tonnes.
